summary: Soshū Nishioka is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held a professorship at International Buddhist University, attested in 2000 and 2015.

Sotan Oka (1860–1921) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bokusan Nishiari, Teizo Shiratori, and Fusho Nagano. He served at Komazawa University as dean/professor (1899) and president (1918), and founded Antai-ji in 1921.

Sras Rinpoche III is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Thubten Kunga, at Drepung Loseling Monastery, and Gyume Tantric Monastery. He held posts at Rizong Monastery, Drepung Loseling (khenpo, 1984), and Gyume Tantric Monastery (1995–2008).

Sravana Borkataky-Varma specializes in religious studies and Indology, holding degrees from the University of Delhi and Rice University (PhD). She has taught at Rice, Montana, UNC Wilmington, Harvard (fellow ~2020–2022), and the University of Houston (~2022).

Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. Educated at Andhra University, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Marburg (PhD ~1963–1966), he served as a professor at Aligarh Muslim University from around 1977 to 1997.

Sri Anirvan (1896–1978) was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He completed his studies at the Sanskrit College and University (~1914–1918), the University of Calcutta, and the University of Dhaka.

Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan (1932–2019) was an Indology scholar who earned his Dr. phil. from the University of Hamburg in 1967. He subsequently served there as Privatdozent für Indologie from 1973 to 1997.

Srisa Chandra Vasu (1861–1918) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Rang Mahal School and Government College University, Lahore. He served as a Vakil at Allahabad High Court (~1883) and founded the Panini Office in 1891.

Stacey Van Vleet works in Tibetology, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She studied under Carole McGranahan and Tashi Tsering Josayma, earned degrees from the University of Colorado and Columbia University (PhD), and held an attested post at Columbia in 2013.

Stamford Raffles (1781–1826) worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He was employed by the East India Company (~1795–1824), founded the Zoological Society of London in 1825, and served as its president in 1826.

Stanislas Julien (1797–1873) was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat and held posts at the Collège de France (Chair of Chinese, 1832–1873), Bibliothèque nationale, and Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales.

Stanislav Grof is a religious studies scholar who studied at Charles University. He held positions at various psychiatric institutes in Prague, Johns Hopkins University, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, Esalen Institute, and the California Institute of Integral Studies (1994–2015).

Stanisław Schayer (1899–1941) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He became a professor at the University of Warsaw in 1922 and was a member of the Warsaw Scientific Society and the Polish Academy of Arts and Sciences.
Stanley Abe works in the fields of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Duke University, attested in 1995 and 2004.

Stanley Insler (1937–2019) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Columbia, Tübingen, and Yale under Paul Thieme, and served as Salisbury Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Yale until 2012.

Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah (1929–2014) was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ceylon, Cornell, and Harvard under Bryce Ryan. He taught at Ceylon, Cambridge, Chicago, and was Rabb Professor of Anthropology at Harvard (1976–2001).

Stanley Lombardo is a scholar of linguistics and philosophy. He studied at Loyola University New Orleans, Tulane University, and the University of Texas at Austin, and held a post at the University of Kansas from ~1976 to 2014.

Stanley Weinstein (1929–2017) specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. Educated at Komazawa, Tokyo, and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, Kodo Sawaki, and Gyokusen Hosaka, he taught at Komazawa, SOAS (1962–1968), and Yale University (1968).

Stanley Wolpert (1927–2019) was an Indology and history scholar educated at City College of New York and the University of Pennsylvania. He spent his academic career at UCLA, serving as assistant professor (1959), associate professor (1963), and department chair (1967–2002).
Stefan Anacker (1939–2021) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1964 to 1970 under the direction of Alex Wayman.
